title: P0 next session: restore bd notes erased by `bd update --notes`; link .beads/PRIME.md
description:
HOW IT WAS FOUND (DAS-Backup-Manager, 2026-10-04): `bd update <id> --notes "..."` REPLACES the whole notes field; `--append-notes` adds an entry. Every log entry written with --notes silently erased the one before it. It surfaced when a read-back of operator decisions recorded minutes earlier (DAS bd 8249) came back missing. bd keeps every version in Dolt (`bd history <id>`), and every committed export keeps one in git: the audit found 35 erased entries on 22 issues there, back to 2026-05 (operator decisions, proofs, diagnoses).
HOW IT WAS FIXED THERE: every entry restored oldest-first, each marked '[restored ...]', ahead of the unchanged current note (DAS commit 5596da7); proven: new value = restored entries + the exact previous value on 22/22 fields, 35/35 entries absent before and present after, live audit 22 fields -> 0. The tool is now ~/.claude/scripts/bd-notes-recover.py (tested both ways on a throwaway bd project, including a write that silently does nothing -> FAIL, exit 2). The house prompt ~/.claude/templates/PRIME.md and ~/.claude/rules/beads.md were corrected the same day.
THIS PROJECT, measured read-only 2026-10-04 13:00 CDT: 2 issues read, 1 erased entry in 1 field(s) on 1 issue(s). Repo: PUBLIC. .beads/PRIME.md: ABSENT (bd default prompt injected each session).
DO AT THE START OF THE NEXT SESSION:
1. `~/.claude/scripts/bd-notes-recover.py audit .` (read-only; exit 1 = erased entries found).
2. If any: `~/.claude/scripts/bd-notes-recover.py restore .` (dry run), then `~/.claude/scripts/bd-notes-recover.py restore . --apply` — it re-reads each field before writing, reads every write back and re-audits; it must end RESTORED AND VERIFIED (exit 0). Then commit the export (.beads/issues.jsonl).
3. Link the house prompt, kept LOCAL (public repo: never commit a home-dir symlink): `ln -s ~/.claude/templates/PRIME.md .beads/PRIME.md && echo .beads/PRIME.md >> .git/info/exclude`; verify `bd prime | grep -c append-notes` prints 1 and `git status` stays clean.
4. From now on: `bd update <id> --append-notes "<date> ..."` for every log entry; `--notes` only to rewrite a field on purpose. Existence checks are three commands (beads.md): `bd search` matches titles and ids only; descriptions need `bd list --all --desc-contains "<word>" --limit 0`.
CLOSE WHEN: the audit exits 0 (after a verified restore if one was needed), the link is in place and `bd prime` shows the --append-notes line. Then delete the P0 block at the top of .claude-checkpoint-notes.md.
notes: 2026-10-04 13:21 Before applying the restore, read the dry-run plan: a note that was rewritten ON PURPOSE comes back too — marked [restored], ahead of the current text, i.e. history, not current truth. That is the intended outcome, but know it before applying.
close_reason: 2026-10-05: audit 1 lost entry (dqi notes) -> restore --apply ended RESTORED AND VERIFIED, re-audit 0 (exit 0). .beads/PRIME.md -> ~/.claude/templates/PRIME.md, excluded via .git/info/exclude; bd prime append-notes count 0 -> 1; git status clean of it.

title: [security] phase 5a reports CLEAN when a scanner fails — 10 sites, including all 3 GitHub alert queries
description:
Every security scanner in phase 5a reports CLEAN when it fails.

Ten call sites share the pattern:

  COUNT=$(tool ... 2>/dev/null | jq '...' || echo "0")
  if [[ "$COUNT" -gt 0 ]]; then  ...found...  else  ...no issues...  fi

Three things conspire, any one sufficient:
  1. 2>/dev/null discards the error, so a human reading the audit output
     never learns the tool complained
  2. || echo "0" substitutes a clean result for a failure
  3. even without (2), || binds to the PIPELINE. If the tool dies, jq gets
     empty input and emits nothing, so COUNT is "" -- and bash evaluates
     [[ "" -gt 0 ]] as false. Prints the checkmark.

DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-24, not inferred:
  GRYPE_COUNT=$(grype dir:/nonexistent-path-xyz --output json 2>/dev/null \
                 | jq '.matches | length' || echo "0")
  -> GRYPE_COUNT=[]  ->  "  OK Grype: No vulnerabilities"

Found because cachyos-sentinel's target/ had grown to 46 GB, which made
grype exceed 3 minutes and get killed. Phase 5a reported that project
grype-clean without grype ever completing a scan.

THE TEN SITES (line numbers at 02d8db8):
  159 DEPENDABOT_COUNT   open Dependabot alerts
  168 CODE_COUNT         open CodeQL alerts
  177 SECRET_COUNT       open secret-scanning alerts
  246 BANDIT_HIGH        Python high-severity
  259 SEMGREP_COUNT      semgrep
  278 CODEQL_ISSUES      local CodeQL SARIF
  316 TRIVY_VULNS        trivy vuln+secret
  328 GRYPE_COUNT        grype
  368 VULN_TOTAL         npm audit
  415 CHECKOV_FAILED     IaC misconfig

The first three are the worst: they are gh api calls, and they are what
enforces the mandatory rule in security.md that ALL GitHub security alerts
be resolved or documented. An expired token, a rate limit, a network blip,
or a repo the token cannot see all return "0 open alerts" and the audit
proceeds as though the baseline were met.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW: the code is idiomatic defensive bash. It reads as
careful error handling. It is the command-v guard's evil twin -- a MISSING
tool being skipped is defensible; a PRESENT tool failing and being reported
clean is worse, because you believe you ran it.

OPERATOR DECISIONS 2026-08-24:
  scope     -- fix all ten, via one shared helper, so an eleventh scanner is
               correct by default
  behaviour -- a failed scanner prints its real stderr, counts toward
               TOTAL_ISSUES, and reports "result UNKNOWN", never clean
  history   -- re-run phase 5a on the active projects once fixed
  timing    -- fix now, before cachyos-sentinel phase 1 starts
notes:
[restored 2026-08-24 17:17:08 — this entry was overwritten by a later `bd update --notes`; recovered from bd history]
SCOPE EXTENDS BEYOND PHASE 5A — found 2026-08-24 while committing the
Step 8 work, by grepping phase-9d for the pattern I had just removed
from 5a.

phase-9d-github.md carries SEVEN more instances:

  221 DEPENDABOT_COUNT=$(echo "$DEPENDABOT_ALERTS" | jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  234 PR_COUNT=$(echo "$DEPENDABOT_PRS"   | jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  246 CODE_COUNT=$(echo "$CODE_ALERTS"    | jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  260 SECRET_COUNT=$(echo "$SECRET_ALERTS"| jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  335 LOCAL_AHEAD=$(git rev-list --count "$REMOTE_BRANCH..HEAD" ... || echo "0")
  336 REMOTE_AHEAD=$(git rev-list --count "HEAD..$REMOTE_BRANCH" ... || echo "0")
  373 FAILED_RUNS=$(gh run list --status failure ... | jq 'length' || echo "0")

The shape differs slightly from 5a's: the tool has already run and its
output sits in a variable, and jq parses that. The consequence is
identical — if the upstream `gh api` returned an error or empty, jq fails
and `|| echo "0"` reports ZERO ALERTS.

So the three GitHub alert queries are swallowed in BOTH phases. Fixing 5a
alone leaves the mandatory security.md baseline unenforced by 9d.

373 deserves its own mention: FAILED_RUNS is how the audit learns CI is
red. A gh failure there reports zero failed runs — the "CI red for 95
commits" incident class, made invisible by the check meant to catch it.

335/336 are the mildest: a git rev-list failure usually means no upstream,
where 0 is defensible. Examine, do not assume.

NOT FIXED. phase-5a's scan_count does not transplant directly, since these
parse an existing variable rather than running a command. Needs either a
sibling helper (parse_count VAR FILTER) or capture-at-source rework so the
gh api failure is caught where it happens.

RESOLVED 2026-08-24 — both halves. 17 sites total.

phase-5a (10 sites): scan_count + scan_failed. Keys on PARSEABILITY, not the
exit code, because bandit/semgrep/checkov/npm-audit all exit non-zero when
they FIND things.

phase-9d (7 sites): gh_json + json_count + audit_unknown.

CORRECTION to this issue's original description, measured rather than
reasoned. The 9d sites went wrong TWO different ways, and only one of them
was the false clean I first described:

  empty stdout (network failure, gh crash, timeout, killed process)
    jq emits nothing, COUNT becomes "", [[ "" -eq 0 ]] is TRUE
    -> "No open alerts". FALSE CLEAN. This is the dangerous one.

  HTTP error carrying a JSON body (401 Bad credentials, 404 Not Found)
    gh writes the error object to STDOUT, so `jq length` counts its KEYS
    -> "3 open alert(s)". PHANTOM ALERTS, and the detail render then
    prints nothing because .[] does not apply to an object.

So an expired token did NOT produce a false clean here; it produced three
imaginary alerts. My earlier note on this issue said otherwise and was
wrong. The 5a half was characterised correctly: those run the tool
directly, the error goes to stderr, stdout is empty, and the result is a
false clean.

Also fixed in passing, same class:
  git rev-list --count ... || echo "0"  (x2) -- a failure made both counts
  zero, which renders as "In sync with remote": a false clean about push
  state, from the step that exists to check push state.
  FAILED_RUNS -- how the audit learns CI is red. A gh failure reported zero
  failed runs: the 95-red-commits incident class, made invisible by the
  check meant to catch it.

TESTS: tests/test-scan-count.sh and tests/test-gh-json.sh, 9 cases each.
Both EXTRACT the helpers from the skill documents, so they exercise
shipping code rather than a copy that can drift. Both were proven able to
fail -- restoring the old swallow turns the failure cases red, and
restoring an exit-code gate turns the nonzero-exit-with-findings case red.

Verified end to end against real gh: a 404 repo now reports
"FAILED - result UNKNOWN, NOT clean / gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)" and counts
an issue; an invalid token reports "gh: Bad credentials (HTTP 401)"; a real
repo still returns count=0 correctly.

REMAINING: re-run phase 5a and 9d against the active projects, per the
operator decision of 2026-08-24. Not yet done.

title: markdownlint: 970 errors across repo markdown (no config existed until 2026-10-05)
description: Found 2026-10-05 while linting the TaskOutput/6.3 commit. The repo had no markdownlint config, so stock MD013 (line length) and MD024 (duplicate headings) fired on every Keep-a-Changelog entry and buried everything else. Added .markdownlint.json (MD013 off, MD024 siblings_only): CHANGELOG.md now lints 0. Remaining with that config: 970 lines of markdownlint output across **/*.md (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 58, README.md 123) — mostly MD040 fence language, MD031/MD032/MD022 blank lines; also one real defect, MD052 at docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:248 '[5][6][7][I]' parsed as an undefined reference link. Fix: markdownlint --fix for the mechanical rules, hand-fix the rest, then gate it in CI. Close when: markdownlint '**/*.md' prints nothing.

title: [zombie] phase-9d Step 8: 'bd preflight' (bd 1.0.3) prints bd's own Go-repo PR checklist, so the phase's orphan grep can never count an orphan
description: Found by the cachyos-sentinel v0.13.0 release's GitHub gate (2026-09-29). skills/test-phases/phase-9d-github.md lines ~511-535 run 'bd preflight' and grep its output for 'orphan'; with bd 1.0.3 embedded mode the command prints a Go test/golangci-lint/Nix-hash checklist for bd's own repository, so the grep finds nothing and ISSUES_FOUND never increments — whatever the real graph state is. Replace with the commands that answer the question: 'bd orphans' (count → ISSUES_FOUND), 'bd lint' and 'bd stale' (informational). Verify both directions: an injected orphan must increment the count. Also update ~/.claude/rules/beads.md's touchpoint line, which calls bd preflight the canonical check.
